expectations.text: Identifies that during the rollout window old code runs against the new schema
expectations.evidence: Once the migration runs, old instances still holding `SELECT ... legacy_email` error on every request

expectations.text: Recommends splitting into separate deploys (expand/contract) rather than shipping the drop with the code
expectations.evidence: Deploy A (Friday): code only... Deploy B (next week): the `DROP`, alone

expectations.text: States that dropping the column is irreversible without a backup or restore
expectations.evidence: Reverting the PR re-adds an *empty* column — the values are gone. The only real restore is point-in-time recovery

expectations.text: Addresses what rollback looks like if the deploy goes wrong
expectations.evidence: The only real restore is point-in-time recovery: snapshot to a side instance, extract, backfill

expectations.text: Addresses the Friday timing in terms of who is available to respond, not as superstition
expectations.evidence: not because it's Friday, but because... it wants people awake, which Friday afternoon isn't

expectations.text: Recommends a CI gate that blocks destructive DDL from landing alongside application code
expectations.evidence: a CI check that fails any PR whose migration contains `DROP`, `TRUNCATE`, or `ALTER ... DROP` unless the PR carries an explicit approval label

expectations.text: Does not approve the merge as-is on the strength of green CI
expectations.evidence: The reversible half is what CI proved

expectations.text: Distinguishes the reversible parts of the change from the irreversible part
expectations.evidence: this PR staples a reversible change (three call sites stop reading a column) to an irreversible one (the column ceases to exist)
